sharedDecision: For caller-provided text that can contain quotes, send the value separately through the database driver's parameter-binding argument rather than incorporating it into query text before execution.

ai200-d-003.stemConditions: Caller category can contain quotation marks; the question expressly requires keeping that value separate from SQL-like query text.

options.text: Use WHERE c.category = @category and pass a parameters entry with name @category and value category.
options.reasoningRole: Only this choice passes the category through a separate parameters entry. The Cosmos-specific @name and name/value array spelling instantiates the shared separation rule.

options.text: Construct the complete WHERE clause by concatenating the caller category into the query string.
options.reasoningRole: Produces literal SQL before query execution instead of a driver parameter. Fixed developer-authored literal SQL is a documented different context; the supplied external caller value is not that context.

options.text: Replace @category in the query string with the caller category before calling query_items.
options.reasoningRole: The visible marker does not create a binding when replaced before query_items. This is another literal-text construction path, not the separate argument channel.

ai200-d-003.explanationComparison: The explanation and deep explanation emphasize separate name/value parameters versus pre-call text replacement. They do not introduce an independent Cosmos-specific eligibility, partition, JSON-value typing or query-operation requirement.

ai200-d-017.stemConditions: Caller title can contain an apostrophe; the cursor and title are supplied and the question expressly asks which call sends the value separately from SQL.

options.text: cur.execute("SELECT id FROM documents WHERE title = '" + title + "'")
options.reasoningRole: The concrete Python concatenation inserts title into SQL text before execute; this is the same erroneous value path as Cosmos B.

options.text: cur.execute("SELECT id FROM documents WHERE title = '%s'" % title)
options.reasoningRole: Python percent formatting resolves the string before execute sees it. It parallels Cosmos C's marker substitution: placeholder-looking text is not driver binding when consumed by host-language formatting.

options.text: cur.execute('SELECT id FROM documents WHERE title = %s', (title,))
options.reasoningRole: Leaves the driver placeholder in SQL and passes the one-element tuple as execute's separate argument. It concretely implements the same value-channel separation as Cosmos A.

ai200-d-017.explanationComparison: The explanation emphasizes the tuple, trailing comma and driver-versus-Python percent processing. Its Cosmos comparison identifies the different API representation but does not itself establish an independent factual decision.

strongestPotentialDistinctionForCoordina: Cosmos uses an @name plus a name/value parameters array; psycopg uses an unquoted %s plus a separate positional tuple, and its wrong formatting option is executable Python. Those are real interfaces, not incorrect claims. d-017 requires more concrete Python syntax interpretation, which is why the existing review preferred it as the representative.
whyTheExistingReviewHeldD003: Despite those true interface differences, both complete option sets make the same external-input/separate-value-channel invariant sufficient to select the only option that sends values separately. Both compare that choice against concatenation and pre-call marker substitution. The Cosmos item is chiefly conceptual prose and does not make another Cosmos-specific rule independently necessary. This is a question-specific semantic judgment, not a rule that all parameterized-query questions in different SDKs must be duplicates.

priorRecommendationForCoordinator.reason: It is the stronger concrete Python formatting/driver-binding exercise at these exact hashes. Both IDs retain existing historical identities, so the preference is about the authored reasoning task rather than simply choosing an older ID.
